how: Starters propose the conversion and the later figure, with the latter also suggesting a feature sequence.
Calls recruit members first to build the figure and later to preserve it against erasure.
Participants answer defence calls by declaring themselves defending or committing to help until sleep.
Participants propose an eight-bit pet, sequence its features, choose foot colours, and suggest a second pet.
An outsider starts the community name and members redo and shrink its letters around neighbouring art.
A concrete build sequence is followed by a report that the figure is done.
Participants identify an intended eye feature and circulate a workplan for another pet.
Members watch the threatened figure and repeatedly repair altered eye pixels.
Keepers erase planned lettering until an explanation reveals its purpose and elicits apologies and cessation.
Participants identify apparent damage as friendly construction and explicitly acknowledge their own mistaken removals.
Reports distinguish unidentified bot recolouring and suspected lost figures from a later denial of responsibility.
An ethical objection to defacing existing art is accepted and followed by admissions, withdrawal, and restoration commitments.
A treaty request receives an offer of pixel help for space and a promise of non-harm.
Former opponents help the new figure and receive an explicit reciprocal commitment.
Members maintain several groups' works without reporting a negotiated exchange.
A visitor carries a treaty proposal into the build thread and receives a negotiating answer.
The initial project calls for converting existing art and schedules an ambush.
Participants declare completion and thank the people who built together.
Participants celebrate survival, dispersed collective work, tiny personal contributions, and enjoyment of defending alongside other projects.
Retrospectives record the ending, lost lettering, and an unrealized second figure.
A screenshot preserves a repaired moment and a timelapse locates the figure's appearance.
Familiar game politics and avatars supply jokes during defence without establishing a shared ideological allegiance.
The canvas-worth component appears as members reassess the activity as fun, warlike, and artistic.
Bot recolouring is reported, but the operators and any adoption of automation by this room remain unidentified.
A proposed joint defence and recalled neighbour protection do not establish a mutually agreed coalition or its organization.
Requests to retain space and non-harm assurances establish bargaining while leaving host jurisdiction and approval rules unresolved.
The documented withdrawal and resizing protect existing art rather than follow erasure of the room's own mark.
Searching for free space and retrospectively reporting few hands do not establish a contemporaneous judgment that the spot could not be held.
Naming proposals, an unfinished pet, and individual renewed interest do not show a collective decision to continue the temporary project.
Sarcastic redesign and colour jokes do not establish a host-wide April Fools takeover or a fictional recruiting call.
A grievance over art destroyed during the canvas event does not establish an inherited pre-canvas quarrel.
Feature sequencing, colour discussion, and consensus show local decisions but cannot test the population frequency claim or establish a command structure.
The conversion target, political joke, and canvas grievance do not identify a pre-existing tie naming an attack rival.
Attribute blame and faction preference to the speaker recalling destroyed art rather than inferring a room-wide adversarial alignment.
Treaty talk, reported consensus, and divergent faction preference do not show stated limits on who can commit the room.
Mourning lettering and sharing a repaired screenshot do not show a dispute over which final record or cleaned version should be authoritative.
Members are invited to live chat and later report defence and lettering work there without exposing the chat's decision process.
People already instructed to protect the figure receive the pixel rule and help locating it.
Hopes that the mark brings people back have one directly reported individual instance without demonstrating collective population growth.
The surviving figure elicits mock names and anatomy jokes without a settled naming decision.
Participants seek free space for the drawing before a documented loss of their own mark.
Participants redo and shrink lettering to accommodate existing neighbouring art rather than relocate after defeat.
Participants explicitly evaluate defacing another person's art as unkind and accept the objection.
Cleaning stray pixels is defended as improving the canvas and challenged as causing stagnation.
Pixel work is fitted between an existing game routine rather than replacing ordinary participation.
A helper bounds participation by the need to sleep.
Using an existing community chat for defence does not establish a new room formed around the canvas mark.
Mock names and anatomy jokes appear without a coded argument over offensive language or hate symbols.
General publicity hopes and lapsed-player recruitment do not identify a creator, company, team, or press outlet being addressed.
Withdrawal because timelapse visibility seems secure and an apology for friendly damage do not establish stressful departure or a repaired personal quarrel.
A public chat invitation and proposed timed ambush do not establish concealed planning or infiltration of rivals' venues.
Admitted friendly removals are explained by misunderstanding rather than resentment of canvas posts.
The ordinary pixel timer and keeping a monitoring tab open do not establish site faults or technical workarounds.
Affection for two fandoms and help across projects do not establish contested dual membership or the room's response to it.
The build call receives concrete sequencing and a later completion report, supporting a local path from recruitment to building.
The starter's proposal can itself recruit helpers, so starting and calling need not occupy separate turns.
The defence call recalls the completed build and names ongoing erasure as the reason for preserving it.
Defence directly prompts neighbour contact and proposals for joint protection and help in return for space.
The later treaty exchange ends in an explicit non-harm promise.
Treat an agreement as one route to restraint because ethical objection and restoration commitments can precede peaceful-neighbour terms.
Recurring repair and unidentified bots do not demonstrate that this room adopted automation because manual defence was insufficient.
Completion and the explicitly remembered shared build supply the achievement celebrated through thanks and collective pride.
Celebration precedes preservation reports, but the concepts do not establish that celebrating caused screenshot or timelapse sharing.
Preservation and individual renewed interest do not establish a collective decision to carry the temporary project forward.
Neighbour protection explains the documented moves while limited manpower is reported after survival rather than as their cause.
Circulating a workplan does not close all design questions because later colours, further pets, and misunderstood lettering remain open.
An outside help appeal receives a short commitment lasting until sleep without establishing the participation of silent readers.
A helper can explicitly condition acceptance on leaving another person's territory rather than offer bare assent.
Help can arise through repaired relations before a later defence crisis rather than depend solely on maintenance strain.
Treaty talk opens a channel for a help-for-space offer and a non-harm promise without verifying subsequent delivery.
Distinguish conditional promises of pixel help or cleaning from evidence that the exchange was performed.
Recruitment and conversion of another work can coincide in the initiating call rather than follow separate stages.
The conversion call elicits reasoned refusal, agreement, and stated efforts to retreat and repair.
The complaint about targeting develops into restoration and explicit terms of peaceful proximity.
The attack's conversational outcome can be repair and a peaceful resolution rather than a continuing hostile contest.
A common-defence proposal and later protection report leave the intervening coalition agreement unobserved.
A hoped-for sticky, chat invitation, and enjoyment of the canvas do not demonstrate a posting flood causing host boundary rules.
Neither post-agreement refusal nor an at-agreement disclaimer of authority is visible in the cited treaty and consensus material.
The friendly-repair mechanism is demonstrated, but the final lettering loss cannot be attributed to failed informing rather than other interference.
A participant may stop maintaining once visibility in a timelapse seems sufficient, even while other people continue defence.
Anticipated timelapse visibility can count as sufficient success before placement ends rather than function only as retrospective preservation.
Pride in the surviving figure coexists with lost lettering and an unfinished second design.
An appeal permits divergent personal responses shaped by earlier canvas experiences rather than binding the whole room to one faction.
Separate hoped-for publicity, an explicitly reported individual return, and chat arrivals whose cause and durability remain unknown.
An invitation and returned work report establish chat coordination without revealing how decisions were made there.
Sparing occupied art makes the subsequent location acceptable to a helper whose participation depends on leaving that territory.
Repair is followed by former opponents helping the new figure and receiving a reciprocal commitment.
Explanation can follow recruitment because a helper receives the protection instruction before learning how the canvas works.
Celebration of survival opens a naming exchange with several playful proposals and no demonstrated final choice.
